title: Telemetry-driven model-bundle recommendations for procurement
creator: Leah Park
description:
Objective: Produce a taxonomy and actionable recommendations that map in-product usage telemetry to procurement-ready 'model bundles' for enterprise buyers. These bundles will balance latency, cost, regulatory constraints (data residency/KMS), and quality.

Why now: Sales and Solutions Engineering report long sales cycles when evaluating model choices for customers with mixed constraints (low-latency APAC, EU data residency, cost-sensitive SMB). We can shorten procurement cycles by surfacing pre-baked bundle recommendations informed by actual usage patterns.

Scope: 1) Define telemetry segments (latency-sensitive, high-throughput, rare-large-context, embedding-heavy). 2) Correlate segments with historical procurement outcomes and support tickets. 3) Produce 6 candidate bundles (e.g., low-latency EU-compliant; cost-optimized quantized; hybrid hosted+dedicated mix) with expected unit economics and risk notes. 4) Deliver a lightweight decision matrix and a short field playbook for AE/SEs.

Data sources: console-usage-summaries (per-route token distribution), billing-ledger, incident-runbook links, enterprise intake notes (Confluence), and Salesforce opportunity tags. Preliminary SQL queries and dashboards are in GH: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops-model-procurement/tree/pm-588213.

Success metrics: Reduction in avg procurement evaluation time from 28 -> 16 days for targeted cohort; +15% win rate on RFPs where we proactively suggested a bundle; internal adoption (>=3 AE/SE pilots).

Deliverables: 1) Telemetry segmentation doc (Confluence: /display/PM/Telemetry+Segments+for+Bundles). 2) 6 bundle spec sheets (CSV + short explainer). 3) Prototype decision endpoint mapping route-level signals to recommended bundles (POC service ticket: ENG-2401). 4) AE playbook and sample slides.

Constraints & trade-offs: - We will prioritize observable telemetry signals to avoid heavy instrumentation changes. - Bundles must be implementable across Hosted/Dedicated/Private; some recommendations will be soft constraints where Private is required. - Privacy: when using usage telemetry tied to customers, ensure pseudonymization and legal sign-off.

Stakeholders: Product (Marco, Leah), Solutions Eng (Priya Shah), Sales (Evan Kim), Legal (Ana Ruiz), Infra Eng (ENG-2401 owner), Console Analytics (ENG-3288).

Risks: telemetry sparsity for small accounts; ambiguous RFIs that hide true latency constraints; model availability changes (version deprecations) requiring bundle maintenance.

Next steps: 1) Run initial segmentation queries and present findings to AE focus group (target 2026-03-12). 2) Validate correlations with 10 closed-won and 10 closed-lost opportunities. 3) Draft 6 bundle specs and circulate for legal/infra review.
